title: Console fidelity decomposition and alpha gatekeeping
creator: Asha Menon
description: Rationalize the initial Console alpha surface by decomposing features into fidelity tiers and gating non-critical telemetry behind an alpha feature flag. Focus areas: dashboards (card set), tracing (sampled traces + lightweight trace details), and route-level cost breakdown (aggregated buckets only). Goal is to ship a small, coherent inspector set that demonstrates core workflows while keeping cost and data volume predictably low.
background: Multiple recent scoping passes have left the alpha Console surface inconsistent across teams and expensive in telemetry. Engineering has flagged tracing ingestion risk and cost spikes from full per-token route cost joins. PM needs a clear cutset and acceptance criteria so alpha can be gated and validated with product metrics before expanding fidelity.
decision_record: We will deliver a two-tier fidelity model: CORE (required for alpha) and ENHANCED (deferred). Core items must be behind an 'alpha_console_core' FF with strict defaults ON for pilot customers. Enhanced items are optional and disabled by default. Tracing will use adaptive sampling (client-side + server-side) to cap trace ingest; full flamegraph-style detail is deferred to ENHANCED. Route cost will be presented in three aggregated buckets: compute, model_tokens, and infra; per-token breakdowns are deferred.
scope_included: Core dashboard: up to 5 insight cards (routes, latency P50/P95, request volume, token spend trend, error rate)
Trace view: sampled spans with metadata, trace timeline visualization (no deep waterfall)
Cost breakdown: route-level aggregated buckets (compute, model_tokens, infra) with daily rollups
Feature flag: alpha_console_core toggle to gate the core surface
Rollout: Gradual enablement for pilot orgs and internal prod testing
scope_removed_or_deferred: High-fidelity trace waterfall and span-level flamegraphs
Per-token and per-operation cost line-items in the initial release
Unlimited dashboard cards and fully configurable card library
Unlimited trace retention; long-tail retention policies deferred to ENHANCED
acceptance_criteria: Alpha core surface enabled by feature flag and deployable to pilot orgs
Total telemetry ingest for Console alpha <= 35% of projected full surface baseline (engineering measured during canary)
Dashboard card set limited to 5 and loads within 800ms on median for pilot orgs under 95th percentile load
Trace sampling reduces span ingest by >= 65% while preserving median latency signal (P50/P95) compared to unsampled traces
Cost breakdown shows aggregated buckets and matches billing within 3% on daily rollups
Product sign-off from Console PM, Observability lead, and Runtime engineering on resource/cost guardrails
rollout_plan: 1) Merge gating FF and core changes behind alpha_console_core. 2) Canary to internal Redwood orgs (2 weeks) with telemetry cost dashboard. 3) Expand to 3 pilot customers with ops monitoring and cost alerts (2–4 weeks). 4) Evaluate telemetry and feedback; unblock ENHANCED work in next cycle if alpha metrics pass.
monitoring_and_telemetry: Create a temporary Console-alpha telemetry dashboard that tracks: overall trace/span ingest, card load latencies, cost delta vs pre-alpha baseline, and alert when cost exceeds 110% of projection. Daily runbook for Eng/PM during canary window.
dependencies_notes: Requires tracing sampling hooks from runtime (ENG-4472 equivalent) and an initial cost rollup job from billing infra. Coordinate with Privacy/Security if any sampled traces include PII fields.
open_questions: What exact sampling ratio should be default for low-volume vs high-volume orgs? (observability asks for adaptive thresholds)
Do we need a secondary FF to enable any ENHANCED cards selectively for enterprise pilots?
Is the three-bucket cost model sufficient for initial QA vs billing reconciliation?
